utterance_starts.first_words: Perdón, señor presidente. La senadora Bar está presente.
Señores senadores: la buena voluntad de esta Presidencia excedió largamente las reglas establecidas
De modo que, senador Menem, queda levantada la sesión por falta de quórum.

notes: The last page of a sitting lifted for want of a quorum: five labels, five turns, and the roll-call being read into the record around them. I set opens_mid_utterance false, and that is the one call I was unsure about. The roll-call plainly continues from the previous page — the first note trails off in an ellipsis ('Agúndez, Baglini, Busti...') and the third resumes with one ('... Chiappe, Colazo...') — but nothing on this page is a continuing paragraph of SPEECH: the page's first line is a fresh dash-opened stenographer's note, so by the brief's test no turn is left dangling from the previous page. If the convention is meant to cover a continuing note as well, this should be true. The chair's second turn runs on in an unlabelled paragraph ('Continúa la toma de lista de los senadores presentes.'), which I did not count as a separate turn. The three roll-call lines and the closing time are each their own paragraph, so all four are events. Two things look defective. First, the running header's page number is typographically broken: instead of 'Pág. 5' the page prints what look like Greek letters — a capital Pi, then 'á', then a gamma — so it reads 'Πáγ. 5'. The rest of the header is normal. Second, senator Menem's turn is cut off in mid-sentence by the chair ('Pido la palabra...'), which is the transcript recording an interruption rather than a defect, but it leaves a turn whose words are three dots and an ellipsis. Also note the sign-off of the Director del Cuerpo de Taquígrafos at the end of the text: it is printed matter, not speech. The bottom half of the page is blank.
